lgd_definition: "Working Dog" shall mean any of various breeds of dogs developed or trained to perform useful work to assist humans (i.e. herding animals, pulling wagons or sleds, or guarding property) and excludes hunting dogs.
collar_tag_req: Every dog Owner shall cause a dog tag to be securely affixed on the dog at all times (until the tag needs replaced).
dog_limit: Limit of three (3) dogs within or about any single detached dwelling, or two (2) dogs per dwelling unit. This limit shall not apply to a property which is zoned Agricultural, possesses a valid kennel license, an approved business and/or veterinary office.
notes: URL: https://ahtwp.squarespace.com/s/BL-133-2019-Animal-Control.pdf. The bylaw is highly farm-friendly. It explicitly defines 'Working Dog' to include both guarding and herding roles, and it completely exempts agriculturally zoned properties from the 3-dog limit. Barking is governed by a separate Noise By-law No. 63-2022 which exempts noises by animals kept or used for agricultural purposes.

collar_tag_req: A dog tag is to be securely fixed on the dog at all times until the tag is renewed or replaced.
dog_limit: No person shall keep or permit to be kept more than three (3) dogs in any one dwelling unit or on any premises in a residential area unless they hold a valid kennel licence.
notes: URL: https://www.amherstburg.ca/media/iv1o4ub3/2022-008-keeping-of-animals-rm.pdf. Standard animal control bylaw without specific exemptions for farm dogs or LGDs. The 3-dog limit specifies 'residential area', suggesting agricultural zones may be implicitly exempt from this restriction.

lgd_definition: "Livestock Guardian Dog" means a purpose bred and trained dog that works and/or lives with domestic farm animals to protect them for predators while aggressively repelling those predators, and is used exclusively for the purpose.
collar_tag_req: Every owner of a dog shall cause a dog tag to be securely affixed on the dog at all times (until the tag needs replaced).
dog_limit: No owner shall keep or permit to be kept more than three (3) dogs at any one time, per dwelling unit, location or residence within the Township of Amaranth, (unless you are on an Agricultural zoned property).
notes: URL: https://www.amaranth.ca/media/x5mbop0o/by-law-2026-08-animal-control-dogs-and-kennels.pdf. Recently updated bylaw that is very farm friendly. It explicitly defines 'Livestock Guardian Dog' and fully exempts agriculturally zoned properties from the 3-dog limit. It also creates a 'Personal Use Kennel' category explicitly for 'Livestock Guardian, Hunting and Predator Control' that allows for additional dogs.

lgd_definition: "Livestock Guardian Dog shall mean a dog that works and/or lives with domestic farm animals to protect them while repelling predators and is used exclusively for that purpose;"
herding_definition: "Herding Dog shall mean a dog that has been trained and is actively being used in a bona fide farming operation for the purposes of controlling livestock on the farm;"
collar_tag_req: The Township is no longer licensing dogs (program discontinued in 2022). Instead, owners must have either a personalized tag with contact information or microchip their dogs.
dog_limit: Residents may keep a maximum of three (3) dogs which are over three (3) months at any one (1) location, unless a kennel license is obtained.
notes: URL: https://www.blandfordblenheim.ca/media/uocbfd43/consolidated-2275-2021-animal-care-and-control.pdf. Contains highly accurate definitions for both LGDs and Herding Dogs. Barking is governed by a separate Noise Control By-law (2357-2023) which exempts normal farm practices.

collar_tag_req: No person shall fail to keep the dog tag securely affixed to the dog for which it was issued, except while the dog is being lawfully used for hunting in the bush, provided the name of the registered owner and their phone number is written on the dog's collar.
dog_limit: No person shall keep or permit to be kept more than three (3) dogs at any premises. However, a person may keep more than three dogs at a premises provided the person is keeping sheep upon the same premises, the premises is on land that is zoned agricultural, and the person provides proof of registration with the Ontario Sheep Marketing Agency.
notes: URL: https://www.brant.ca/media/htqpbujq/animal-control.pdf. Uniquely provides a specific exemption to the 3-dog limit for farmers keeping sheep on agriculturally zoned land. The County's online dog licensing portal also explicitly lists 'Herding Dogs' as an exemption category.

collar_tag_req: All dogs in Burlington must be licensed and wear the identification tag issued by the City.
dog_limit: Residents are allowed to own a maximum of 4 animals total (cats or dogs) per residence. This limit does not apply to properties outside of the Urban Planning Area.
notes: URL: https://www.burlington.ca/en/by-laws-and-animal-services/resources/By-laws/By-law-Search/060-2005-By-law.pdf. Agricultural properties located outside the Urban Planning Area are implicitly exempted from the strict animal caps. Barking is governed by the Nuisance and Noise Control By-law (019-2003).

lgd_definition: “Livestock Guardian Dog” (LGD) means a dog that works with domestic farm animals for protection from predators and is used exclusively for that purpose.
herding_definition: “Herding Dog” means a dog that has been trained and is actively being used in a bona fide farming operation for the purpose of controlling livestock.
collar_tag_req: Livestock Guardian Dog or Herding Dog shall be exempt from wearing a collar or tag, provided that the Owner has paid the annual licensing fee, registered said dog with the Township and provided identifying information for the dog from an ear tattoo, micro-chip, and/or proof of membership with the Canadian Kennel Club.
dog_limit: Maximum of 3 dogs per property. However, Working Dogs, Herding Dogs and LGDs are excluded from the definition of a 'Dog' in the bylaw entirely, explicitly exempting them from the limit.
notes: URL: https://www.townshipofbrock.ca/media/rvwhdxuh/2446-2012-pp-animal-control-bylaw-accessible.pdf. Highly accommodating to farmers. It explicitly defines LGDs and Herding Dogs, and exempts them from having to wear a physical collar or tag while working (provided they are microchipped or tattooed) to protect them from snagging or injuries from predators.

collar_tag_req: All dogs (older than 12 weeks/4 months of age) residing within the City of Cambridge are to be licensed and have their license tag affixed at all times.
dog_limit: Maximum of three (3) dogs on property. Keeping more than three dogs requires a kennel licence.
notes: A strictly urban-focused by-law enforced by the Cambridge & District Humane Society. No exemptions or specific provisions for farm dogs or LGDs were found.

collar_tag_req: Every person who is provided with a tag... shall ensure that the tag is affixed to the collar of the dog in such a manner that the tag can identify such dog to any person at all times.
dog_limit: Maximum of three (3) dogs within any single detached dwelling, or two (2) dogs per dwelling unit. These limits shall not apply to a property which is zoned Agricultural, possesses a valid kennel license, or an approved veterinary office.
notes: URL: https://www.cavanmonaghan.net/media/kjfbhhqi/by-law-no-2023-85.pdf. Extremely farm-friendly by broadly exempting all properties zoned Agricultural from the standard 3-dog limit. Noise By-law No. 2022-21 excludes noises generated by farm equipment and animals.

herding_definition: “Farm Dog” means a dog which is actively herding farm animals on agricultural property, such as cattle or sheep;
collar_tag_req: An owner of a dog shall keep the tag issued by the Township securely fixed on the dog for which it was issued at all times.
dog_limit: No person shall keep or harbour or permit to be kept or harboured at any one time, more than three (3) dogs on a property. This limit does not apply to the owner of an Agricultural property that is actively being used for agricultural purposes.
notes: URL: https://www.centrewellington.ca/media/32rgywui/19-70.pdf. The bylaw defines 'Farm Dog' to include herding dogs and exempts them from 'running at large' restrictions if active in their trained duties. It also explicitly exempts actively used agricultural properties from the 3-dog limit.
